contents.name: 6.1 A zero-free region

contents.name: Lemma 6.2 (The Borel–Carathéodory Lemma)
contents.reason: This general analytic real-part-to-modulus estimate belongs to complex analysis; the chosen global Hadamard argument and already-published local zeta formula supply the required estimates without invoking it.

contents.name: Lemma 6.3 (logarithmic derivative from nearby zeros)
contents.reason: The general disc theorem is an alternative analytic foundation for Lemma 6.4. Its zeta specialization is already established in lem-local-logarithmic-derivative-zeta; no unproved version of the general theorem is used here.

contents.name: Lemma 6.4 (local logarithmic derivative of zeta)
contents.support: Published local formula uses a unit ordinate window instead of this disc; both give the needed high-height O(log t) remainder.

contents.name: Lemma 6.5 (the 3,4,1 inequality)
contents.support: Nonnegative Lambda coefficients give the shifted derivative inequality.

contents.name: Theorem 6.6 (classical zero-free region)
contents.support: Pole-versus-nearby-zero comparison; bounded heights handled independently.

contents.name: Nonnegative cosine polynomials and the Fejér kernel (unnumbered discussion)
contents.reason: Optimizing the coefficient ratio toward two improves numerical constants only. The assigned classical existence theorem needs the fixed 3,4,1 polynomial, whose entire argument is included.

contents.name: Theorem 6.7 (bounds within the zero-free region)
contents.support: High-height derivative comparison supports a logarithmic bound and integration controls the reciprocal; low-height pole subtraction is explicit.

contents.name: Theorem 6.8 (zeros in a disc centered at 1+it)
contents.support: A zero contributes a reciprocal-radius amount to a positive real-part sum.

contents.name: Dirichlet L-functions and function-dependent constants (unnumbered paragraph)
contents.support: The text distinguishes individual functions from the later systematic modulus-dependent treatment.

contents.name: 6.2 The prime number theorem
contents.support: Truncation and a logarithmic zero-free boundary balance at exponential square-root height.

contents.support: Quantitative psi estimate from the finite rectangle.

contents.name: Theorem 6.9, equation (6.13): theta error
contents.support: Discard prime powers using the Chebyshev bound.

contents.name: Theorem 6.9, equation (6.14): pi and li
contents.support: Partial summation with lower endpoint retained.

contents.name: li(x) integral convention (unnumbered definition)
contents.support: Integral starts at two.

contents.name: Asymptotic expansion (6.15)
contents.support: Repeated integration by parts gives factorial coefficients.

contents.name: Theorem 7.14 (absolute values of number fields)
contents.support: Places are classified modulo equivalence; use ordinary complex modulus as representative, not its square.

contents.name: Theorem 7.38
contents.support: Discrete separable complete-field extension and norm formula; the general claim requires the separately read Conrad treatment.

contents.name: Remark 7.39
contents.support: The source explicitly states that nondiscrete and archimedean existence need a different omitted proof; Conrad supplies the general finite nonarchimedean proof.

contents.name: Corollary 7.40
contents.reason: Extension to an arbitrary separable algebraic extension is an infinite-extension result; the design requests finite extensions, for which the preceding theorem supplies all needed absolute values.

contents.name: Remark 7.41
contents.reason: The discussion of C_p and abstract field isomorphisms concerns completed algebraic closures and additional choice issues, beyond finite number-field completions. Its algebraic-closedness claim needs the algebraic-closure hypothesis and is not imported for arbitrary Omega.

contents.name: Corollary 7.42
contents.support: The local degree equals e f. The planned theorem proves the number-field-completion case using the global stabilizer and preserves local e,f by density.

contents.name: Remark 7.43 (normalization of extended valuations)
contents.support: The base integer-valued valuation extends with value group (1/e)Z; distinguish the normalized upper valuation from its extending rescaling.

contents.name: Proposition 8.13
